channel.title: toriku.wtf blog
channel.description: Creative AI, rights, film and filmmaking in Mexico.

item.title: Creative AI: from script to storyboard without losing your voice
item.description: How to use artificial intelligence in a short film's pre-production as an assistant, not an author: ideas, script, storyboard, previsualization and animatic.

item.title: When is it ethical to use AI in a short film? A practical guide
item.description: Clear criteria to decide when artificial intelligence adds value and when it crosses a line: consent, voices, faces, training data and transparency.

item.title: Monetizing AI-made videos on YouTube: what works and what does not
item.description: YouTube's inauthentic content policy does not ban AI: it penalizes repetitive, mass-produced videos. What to check before joining the Partner Program.

item.title: How to make money with a short film in Mexico
item.description: Festivals with prizes, platforms, TV, brands, public funds and services: the real routes for a Mexican short to earn back what it cost.

item.title: Industry standards: DCP, color, audio and subtitles
item.description: What festivals, cinemas and platforms ask for when you deliver a short: DCP, color space, loudness, subtitles and paperwork. A checklist so delivery does not fail.

item.title: AI standards in the industry: unions, contracts and content credentials
item.description: What the WGA and SAG-AFTRA set out on AI, what C2PA content credentials are, and how to adopt those rules in Mexican productions.

item.title: Film copyright in Mexico: who owns your short?
item.description: Who the authors of an audiovisual work are under Mexico's copyright law, what the producer acquires, moral and economic rights, INDAUTOR registration and basic contracts.

item.title: AI-made works in Mexico: what the Supreme Court decided
item.description: The SCJN's Amparo directo 6/2025 and the 2026 copyright reform on voice and likeness: what can be registered, what cannot and how to protect your work.

item.title: Audiovisual intellectual property in Spain: a guide for Latin American creators
item.description: Authors of an audiovisual work under Spain's LPI, assignment to the producer, collecting societies (SGAE, DAMA, AISGE, EGEDA), the quotation right and Spain's new AI law.

item.title: US copyright for Mexican creators: registration, fair use and AI
item.description: How US copyright works for a Mexican short: registration, work made for hire, fair use, public domain and AI-assisted works.

item.title: Audiovisual copyright in Latin America: a quick map
item.description: Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Peru and the Andean Community: term, author remuneration and AI for co-producing and distributing shorts in the region.

item.title: How to make a video essay without infringing copyright (and get it watched)
item.description: Quotation in Mexico, the quotation right in Spain and fair use in the US: how much third-party footage to use in a video essay, how to structure it and how to respond to Content ID.

item.title: The film market in Mexico: 2025 figures and what they mean for a creator
item.description: Attendance, box office, insecurity and streaming: what IMCINE's yearbook says about Mexican cinema and how to read it if you make shorts.

item.title: Mexico's 2026 Federal Law of Film and Audiovisual Media: what changes for creators
item.description: The law that replaces the 1992 one: a 10 % screen quota, 14 days in theaters, a Mexican cinema section on platforms and human dubbing.

item.title: Financing your short in Mexico: public funds, incentives and alternatives
item.description: IMCINE and state calls, creation grants, tax incentives, co-production, brands and crowdfunding for Mexican short films.

item.title: Film festivals in Mexico for short filmmakers: map and strategy
item.description: Morelia, Guadalajara, Guanajuato, FICUNAM, Ambulante, Shorts México and more: how to choose which festivals to send your short to, and in what order.

item.title: FICM 2026: what the Morelia winners leave us
item.description: «Seis meses en el edificio rosa con azul», «Cuerda manual» and «Forensita»: what Morelia 2026 rewarded and what short filmmakers can learn.

item.title: How to open a legal film club in Mexico: rights, licenses and permits
item.description: What the law says about public screenings, why «non-profit» is not enough, how to get licenses, ratings, music and venue permits.

item.title: Programming a film club: public domain, open licenses and Mexican cinema
item.description: Which films you can screen, why the public domain arrives late in Mexico, how to use Creative Commons licenses and how to build series with Mexican shorts.

item.title: Writing a short film: structure in ten pages
item.description: How to write a short that works: a single idea, a character with a want, a twist and an ending that stays with you. Exercises and common mistakes.

item.title: Lighting a short film on a low budget
item.description: Natural light, bounces, practicals and a couple of LED panels: how to get a cinematic image without a truck full of gear.

item.title: Location sound: the mistake that most gives away an amateur short
item.description: Microphones, ambience, room tone and on-set habits to record clean dialogue. Why audiences forgive an imperfect image but not bad sound.

item.title: Shooting a film on your phone: settings, accessories and workflow
item.description: How to get a cinematic image from a phone: manual mode, frame rate, shutter, color profiles, stabilization, sound and editing.

item.title: Filming in Mexico City: permits, locations and safety
item.description: When you need notice or a permit to film on Mexico City's public streets, monuments, transport, drones, insurance and how to work with neighbors.

item.title: Movie releases in Mexico: November 2026
item.description: The films reaching Mexican cinemas in November 2026: Mexican cinema, big franchises, animation and documentaries. With notes for filmmakers.

item.title: «Atrápelo quien pueda»: Jaime Camil's romantic comedy reaches cinemas
item.description: Released November 12, 2026: director, cast, story, production and why romantic comedy is still key to Mexican cinema's box office.

item.title: «The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping»: what to expect from the release
item.description: The Haymitch prequel arrives in November 2026 with Francis Lawrence directing. Cast, story and what a filmmaker can learn from a prequel.

item.title: GTA VI arrives on November 19: what matters to video creators
item.description: Date, platforms, pre-load and why GTA VI is also an audiovisual phenomenon: trailers, cinematic storytelling and the wave of content to come.

item.title: GTA VI clips for social media: capture, editing and rights
item.description: How to capture, edit and publish GTA VI clips in vertical and horizontal: console settings, editing, music, Content ID and Rockstar's policy.
